gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have known you were in hospital — nobody told me.
gaps.explanation: 'Couldn't have' means it was impossible to do: couldn't have known.

gaps.sentence: It ___ be the postman — he has already been this morning.
gaps.hint: ruled out by what already happened
gaps.explanation: Evidence that rules something out uses 'can't': can't be.

gaps.sentence: Although the road was blocked, we ___ reach the hospital in time.
gaps.explanation: For a single past achievement, 'was/were able to' is used, not 'could'.

gaps.sentence: It was careless of her — she ___ have prepared more thoroughly for the interview.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' criticizes a failure to act properly: should have prepared.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not agree, but let us ask him anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'May' expresses a possibility about the future: may not agree.

gaps.sentence: You ___ told me — I would have kept the evening free!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' plus the participle criticizes something that did not happen: should have told.
